text:
San Jose arrives 1-3-1 in its last five and fresh off a shootout loss to Pittsburgh, where Mason Marchment reached 100 career goals and Macklin Celebrini hit 200 career points. Utah is winless in four (0-2-2), most recently a 1-0 shootout loss to St. Louis, and it is short Logan Cooley, Dylan Guenther and Nate Schmidt. Clayton Keller has slid in beside Trocheck and Crouse, and Kailer Yamamoto's minutes have jumped to 19:13 a night from 13:22. Utah's skid is real by the chances: 42% of the expected goals, the quality of shots taken and allowed.

Our numbers favor the home side, 3.74 expected goals to 2.87. At five on five Utah has taken 57% of the expected goals this season, San Jose 45%, and the Sharks' penalty kill allows 1.0 expected goals a game against Utah's 0.72. In net, Yaroslav Askarov (projected) is +7.0 goals saved above expected, meaning he has stopped more than an average goalie would have faced with the same shots, after -19.4 last season. Karel Vejmelka (projected) is at -4.3 this year after +5.4 last.

Celebrini is our top San Jose scorer at 43%, and Will Smith, one goal from 50 career goals, is at 34%. Keller leads Utah at 33%. Nick Schmaltz is day-to-day, so check the lineup. Among our under-the-radar picks, Jack McBain's third-line shots have been dangerous, with 2.0 expected goals over his last 10 games, and we have him at 17% to score. Yamamoto is 49% for a point on added ice time.
